## Demo

```{python}
#| output: asis
import json, os
manifest = json.load(open("output/manifest.json"))
# order: gibbons (Chiba clips by number, then grooming2) with the chimpanzee/bonobo clips spread evenly among them
import re
gib = sorted([m for m in manifest if m["name"].startswith(("Gibbons", "grooming"))],
             key=lambda m: int(re.search(r"_(\d+)_", m["name"]).group(1)) if m["name"].startswith("Gibbons") else 99)
apes = sorted([m for m in manifest if m not in gib], key=lambda m: m["name"])
step = (len(gib) + len(apes)) / max(len(apes), 1)
slots = {round(step * (i + 0.5)) for i in range(len(apes))}
ordered, gi, ai = [], iter(gib), iter(apes)
for k in range(len(gib) + len(apes)):
    ordered.append(next(ai) if k in slots else next(gi, None) or next(ai))
manifest = ordered
print(f"<script>const MANIFEST = {json.dumps(manifest)};</script>")
```

```{=html}
<style>
  #viewer { max-width: 960px; }
  #viewer .controls { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .5rem 1rem; align-items: center; margin-bottom: .6rem; }
  #viewer select { max-width: 26rem; }
  #viewer .seg { display: inline-flex; border: 1px solid #adb5bd; border-radius: .4rem; overflow: hidden; }
  #viewer .seg button { border: 0; background: transparent; padding: .25rem .7rem; cursor: pointer; }
  #viewer .seg button.on { background: #2780e3; color: #fff; }
  #viewer video { width: 100%; background: #000; border-radius: .3rem; }
  #viewer .info { font-size: .85rem; color: #6c757d; margin-top: .3rem; }
</style>
<div id="viewer">
  <div class="controls">
    <button id="prev" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" title="previous (←)">◀</button>
    <select id="sample" class="form-select form-select-sm"></select>
    <button id="next" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" title="next (→)">▶</button>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <span>smoothing</span><span class="seg" id="level"></span>
    <span>draw</span><span class="seg" id="style"></span>
    <button id="sound" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary">🔇 sound off</button>
  </div>
  <video id="video" controls autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
  <div class="info" id="info"></div>
</div>
<script>
(() => {
  const levels = ["none", "low", "medium", "high"], styles = ["points", "skeleton"];
  let s = 0, level = "low", style = "points";
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id), vid = $("video");
  MANIFEST.forEach((m, i) => $("sample").add(new Option(m.name, i)));
  function seg(el, opts, get, set) {
    opts.forEach(o => { const b = document.createElement("button"); b.textContent = o;
      b.onclick = () => { set(o); show(true); }; el.appendChild(b); });
    return () => [...el.children].forEach(b => b.classList.toggle("on", b.textContent === get()));
  }
  const markLevel = seg($("level"), levels, () => level, v => level = v);
  const markStyle = seg($("style"), styles, () => style, v => style = v);
  function show(keepTime) {
    const m = MANIFEST[s], t = keepTime ? vid.currentTime : 0;
    $("sample").value = s; markLevel(); markStyle();
    const muted = vid.muted;
    vid.src = m.levels[level].videos[style];
    vid.muted = muted;                                              // keep the sound setting across switches
    vid.addEventListener("loadedmetadata", () => { vid.currentTime = Math.min(t, vid.duration || t); }, { once: true });
    $("info").textContent = `${m.file} · ${m.width}×${m.height} · ${m.fps} fps in → ${m.fps_out} fps out · ` +
      `${m.frames_in} frames in, ${m.frames_out} out · ${m.seconds} s · ${m.size_mb} MB · apes tracked: ${m.levels[level].apes}`;
  }
  $("sound").onclick = () => { vid.muted = !vid.muted;
    $("sound").textContent = vid.muted ? "🔇 sound off" : "🔊 sound on"; vid.play(); };
  vid.addEventListener("volumechange", () => { $("sound").textContent = vid.muted ? "🔇 sound off" : "🔊 sound on"; });
  $("sample").onchange = e => { s = +e.target.value; show(false); };
  $("prev").onclick = () => { s = (s - 1 + MANIFEST.length) % MANIFEST.length; show(false); };
  $("next").onclick = () => { s = (s + 1) % MANIFEST.length; show(false); };
  document.addEventListener("keydown", e => { if (e.target.tagName === "SELECT") return;
    if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") $("prev").click(); if (e.key === "ArrowRight") $("next").click(); });
  show(false);
})();
</script>
```

## Installation

GPU (NVIDIA):

```bash
conda create -n apetrack python=3.11 -y
conda activate apetrack
pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126
pip install envisionboxbio-apetrack
```

CPU only:

```bash
conda create -n apetrack python=3.11 -y
conda activate apetrack
pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
pip install envisionboxbio-apetrack
```

## Tracking apes

```python
from envisionboxbio_apetrack import ApeTracker

tracker = ApeTracker()                                   # default settings
tracker.process_video("clip.mp4", "output/")             # one video
tracker.process_folder("videos/", "output/")             # every video in a folder

# other settings, e.g.
tracker = ApeTracker(box_smoothing="medium", keypoint_smoothing="medium", draw=("skeleton", "points"))
```

Per video: `<name>_tracks.csv` (one row per ape per frame: box, track ID, 16 keypoints with likelihood),
`<name>_skeleton.mp4` / `<name>_points.mp4`, and `<name>_detections.csv` (raw detections, reused when you
re-run with other tracking or smoothing settings).

## How videos are transformed

| | output |
|---|---|
| frame rate | same as the input (e.g. 25 fps in → 25 fps out); one output frame and one CSV frame index per input frame |
| resolution | same as the input unless `output_width` is set (the demo uses 960); CSV coordinates always in input pixels |
| interlaced video | deinterlaced, one frame per frame (frame rate unchanged) |
| audio | copied into the labelled videos |
| codec | H.264 .mp4 |

The demo videos, measured:

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown
df = pd.DataFrame([{"video": m["file"], "size": f'{m["width"]}×{m["height"]}', "fps in": m["fps"], "fps out": m["fps_out"],
                    "frames in": m["frames_in"], "frames out": m["frames_out"]} for m in manifest])
Markdown(df.to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Settings

```{python}
import dataclasses
from envisionboxbio_apetrack import Config, SMOOTHING
rows = [{"setting": f.name, "default": repr(f.default if f.default is not dataclasses.MISSING else f.default_factory())}
        for f in dataclasses.fields(Config) if f.name != "extra"]
Markdown(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False) + "\n\nSmoothing windows (seconds, Savitzky-Golay order 2): " +
         ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in SMOOTHING.items()))
```

## Under the hood

```{python}
#| output: asis
import inspect
from envisionboxbio_apetrack import config, detect, pose, smooth, track, tracker

def dropdown(title, *objs):
    code = "\n\n".join(inspect.getsource(o) for o in objs)
    print(f"<details><summary><b>{title}</b></summary>\n\n```python\n{code}\n```\n\n</details>\n")

dropdown("The whole pipeline (ApeTracker.process_video)", tracker.ApeTracker.process_video)
dropdown("Models: OWLv2 detector (prompts, fp16, tiles)", detect.OWLv2Detector)
dropdown("Models: OpenApePose (HRNet-W48, weights, flip test)", pose.OpenApePose, pose.load_model, pose.keypoints_for_boxes)
dropdown("Settings (Config)", config)
dropdown("Tracking: ByteTrack, stitching, gap filling", track.bytetrack, track.stitch_tracks, track.fill_gaps)
dropdown("Smoothing: boxes and keypoints", smooth)
```
